Structure
The plot of TL is as follows: we find the narrator under a tree on a hill, where he has spent
the night awake, deep in thought. The sun rises and the narrator turns his back to it, at
which point he is overcome by the trance-like state in which he experiences his vision. In
this vision, the narrator is by the side of a public way on a summer’s evening, and observes
a large crowd moving seemingly at random. This multitude grows more wild and chaotic,
before a chariot guided by a Janus-faced shadow (with its eyes covered) approaches, car-
rying an ethereal figure within it. The crowd gives way to the chariot and becomes even
more agitated; the chariot is then compared to a Roman triumphal procession, and we
are told that the chariot has a separate crowd that it drives along in captivity. The narrator
describes the captives as those who had been powerful in their lifetime and had acquired
